title: Module quiz: Claude for every role

questions.stem: Two staff members each receive a readable draft from Claude: a lesson rubric for one, a funding appeal for the other. Which pair of checks matches what each of them owns?

options.text: First: reading level and layout; second: tone and brand voice
options.says: Ruled out because the educator's checks include "alignment with the stated outcome", which reading level and layout do not cover, and they leave out "accuracy of the content taught".

options.text: First: pupils' reactions once it is handed out; second: donors' reactions once it is sent
options.says: Ruled out because the educator "Owns: what students are taught, how they are assessed and the fairness of grades", and the fundraiser must check "every claim about impact, every statistic and every funder requirement against the source" before the audience reacts.

options.text: First: accuracy and outcome fit; second: impact claims against sources
options.says: The educator checks accuracy and alignment with the outcome, and the fundraiser checks impact claims against the source.

options.text: First: Claude's own rating of its accuracy; second: Claude's own rating of its sources
options.says: Ruled out because the page lists "Impact claims and statistics against source" as the check that matters most, and a self-rating is not a comparison with a source.

questions.stem: A freelancer working for a charity wants Claude to write personalised thank-you notes that cite each supporter's past gifts, working from the full supporter list. Charity policy says personal data may not leave its systems unprotected. What should happen first?

options.text: Send twenty complete records to test the tone of the notes
options.says: Ruled out because "the best answer anonymises or aggregates first and checks results", and twenty complete records are still personal data.

options.text: Strip names and addresses, then use templates with merge fields
options.says: Donor records are sensitive, so identifiers come out before the data goes anywhere, and the notes can be merged afterwards.

options.text: Pick a faster, cheaper model, since thanks are low-stakes drafting
options.says: Ruled out because "high-volume, low-stakes drafting suits a faster, cheaper model" is about cost, and the data class is unchanged by the tier.

options.text: Ask Claude to confirm that it will not keep the supporters' details
options.says: Ruled out because "Donor and beneficiary records are sensitive" and the rule is to "classify first, remove identifiers before analysis", which a promise from the tool does not replace.

questions.stem: A student's course bans AI help on a graded essay. A freelance illustrator's commission contract is silent on AI. Both are tempted to use Claude. What fits each of them?

options.text: The first leaves it out; the second uses it for production and says what was done
options.says: Where a setting has a rule, follow it; where it has none, say what you did, and a maker delegates production while keeping authorship.

options.text: The first uses it for planning only; the second uses it and says so
options.says: Ruled out because "When the setting has a rule about AI help, follow it", and a ban leaves no room for planning help.

options.text: The first leaves it out; the second uses it and says nothing unless a client asks
options.says: Ruled out because "Disclosure matters more here than in many fields", and the maker answers for audiences' and commissioners' expectations.

options.text: The first leaves it out; the second uses it freely and stays silent, as the contract says nothing
options.says: Ruled out because the page says that when a setting has no rule, "say what you did".

questions.stem: Claude turns a wholesaler's data sheet into allergen notes for a bakery's new product line. One note says "may contain nuts" for an item that the sheet marks nut-free. What should the owner do?

options.text: Treat it as a one-off slip and correct only that item
options.says: Ruled out because a small owner builds in "a short list of facts to verify before sending", which means checking the whole notice, not one item.

options.text: Ask Claude to explain how it reached that note, then trust the rest
options.says: Ruled out because the check is "that an answer matches the actual policy and not a plausible one", and an explanation from the same tool is not that comparison.

options.text: Check every statement against its source before anything goes out
options.says: A statement customers rely on is checked against the source, and one error shows the rest are unproven.

options.text: Add a line saying an AI drafted it, and publish the rest unchanged
options.says: Ruled out because "the draft is the start of the judging", and a disclosure line does not correct any statement.
